memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make a table of acacia wood — two cubits long, a cubit wide and a cubit and a half high. Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding around it. Also make around it a rim a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim." - Exodus 25:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Next God describes a table — beautifully made of acacia wood, overlaid in pure gold, finished with careful moulding and a protective rim. This table would stand in the Holy Place and hold bread continually before the Lord. Even a piece of furniture was crafted with dignity and beauty, because it belonged to God.

Notice the rim around the edge. It was a practical detail, designed to keep what was on the table from sliding off. God's instructions were not only beautiful but thoughtful. He cares about how things are made, and about things being made well. Excellence and care in ordinary work are not beneath God's notice; they honour Him.

There is quiet encouragement here for whatever your hands do. Whether you cook, build, teach, drive, clean, or manage accounts, the care you put into ordinary work can be an offering to God. Paul urges us to work at whatever we do with our whole heart, as working for the Lord (Col 3:23). The craftsmen who made this table were doing holy work, though they were simply shaping wood and hammering gold. So is your work today, when it is done for Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I bring care and excellence to my ordinary daily work?
How would my attitude change if I worked today as if directly for God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You care about beauty and craftsmanship even in ordinary things. Help me do my daily work with care and wholeheartedness, offering it to You as worship. Amen.
